item.title: Extensions of a family of Linear Cycle Sets whose underlying group is a product of two cyclic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.33192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use the linear cycle set cohomology in order to compute extensions of a non trivial linear cycle sets whose underlying additive group is a product of two cyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Guccione, Juan Jos\'e Guccione, Christian Valqui

item.title: A crystallographic quotient of the framed braid group and associated flat manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.33308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the quotient of the framed braid group $FB_n$ by the commutator subgroup of the framed pure braid group $FP_n$. We prove that $$ \frac{FB_n}{[FP_n,FP_n]}\cong\mathbb Z^n\rtimes\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}, $$ and, for $n\geq3$, that this quotient is a crystallographic group of dimension $n(n+1)/2$ with holonomy group $S_n$. We investigate its finite-order elements and conjugacy classes, prove that it has no elements of finite even order, and construct Bieberbach subgroups with prescribed finite $2$-group holonomy. Starting from suitable Bieberbach subgroups of $\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}$, we then construct Bieberbach subgroups of the framed quotient whose associated compact flat manifolds are torus bundles over the corresponding unframed flat manifolds. We describe these bundles through the generalized Calabi construction and determine their orientability, first Betti numbers, and the centers of their fundamental groups. As an application, we study a family with cyclic holonomy of odd order, obtaining a criterion for the existence of flat K\"ahler structures, and indicate how the same construction applies to cyclic holonomy of $2$-power order.
item.dc:creator: \^Enio Leite, Oscar Ocampo, Paulo Cesar Cerqueira dos Santos J\'unior, Ana Carolina Moura Teixeira

item.title: Absolutely universal projective embeddings of long-root geometries of orthogonal type
item.description: arXiv:2610.33384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $\Gamma$ its long-root geometry, namely $\Gamma$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $\Gamma$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $\Gamma$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $\Gamma$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $\Gamma$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $\Gamma$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $\Gamma$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $\Gamma$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Pasini

item.title: Counterexamples to congruences in finite p-groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.33615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a conjugacy class of a finite $p$-group $G$. H\'ethelyi, K\"ulshammer and the author asked whether the number of conjugacy classes contained in $KK^{-1}$ is always congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$, and whether, dually, the number of irreducible constituents of $\chi\overline{\chi}$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$ for every $\chi\in\mathrm{Irr}(G)$. We construct a group of order $7^7$ for which both congruences fail.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Sambale

item.title: On the isomorphism problem of Cayley digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.33692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A finite group $G$ is called a DCI-group provided any two Cayley digraphs $Cay(G,S)$ and $Cay(G,T)$ are isomorphic iff the two connection sets $S$ and $T$ are images of each other via automorphisms of the group $G$. Building on the vast literature on CI- and DCI-groups we present an updated list of possible DCI-groups. In addition, we give an alternative proof that does not rely on deep results from group theory. We also point out the three most important open problems related to the classification of DCI-groups.
item.dc:creator: P\'eter P. P\'alfy

item.title: On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.33978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known. In this paper, we determine the possible structures of automorphism groups $X$ of connected 2-arc-transitive Cayley graphs $\Gamma$ of $G\cong T^k$, where $T$ is a finite nonabelian simple group and $k\geqslant2$. In the quasiprimitive case, we prove that $G\unlhd X$, $\Gamma$ is complete, or $X$ is of product action type with restricted parameters. For the non-quasiprimitive case, we determine the possible structures of the quasiprimitive normal quotients of $\Gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Feng Deng, Jing Jian Li, Hao Yu

item.title: Word Trace Formulas over Compact Groups and Connected Cumulants
item.description: arXiv:2610.34213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the expected value of the product of traces for a finite set of words within any compact subgroup of $\mathcal(N)$. Furthermore, we establish a sufficient condition under which these values determine that the product of the conjugacy classes of the words contains the identity.
item.dc:creator: Liviu Paunescu, Florin Radulescu

item.title: The measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups
item.description:
arXiv:2610.34323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we show that all the nonamenable Baumslag-Solitar groups with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree, i.e., $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ with $|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p|
eq |q|$, are measure equivalent to each other, thereby completing the measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups: each $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ belongs to one of three measure equivalence classes according to whether it is amenable ($|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$), virtually isomorphic to $\mathbf{F}_n 	imes \mathbf{Z}$ ($|p|=|q|
eq 1$), or is nonamenable with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree ($|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p| 
eq |q|$). More generally, we obtain the similar classification of the generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups of rank $1$ (i.e., groups that act cocompactly on a tree with edge and vertex stabilizers infinite cyclic). Our proof also establishes a classification of all treeable lcsc groups into exactly six measure equivalence classes. Our new contribution which completes this taxonomy is: all nonunimodular nonamenable treeable lcsc groups are measure equivalent. Along the way we obtain several results about type $\mathrm{III}$ equivalence relations and graphings of independent interest. For example, we show that every ergodic type $\mathrm{III}_0$ graphing admits an ergodic hyperfinite subgraph for which the natural factor map of Krieger flows is an isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Damien Gaboriau, Antoine Poulin, Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob, Konrad Wr\'obel

item.title: Chain flaring fails on the rose for atoroidal irreducible automorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.34571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the chain flare condition introduced by Clay fails for every topological representative on the topological $n$-rose of every power of an atoroidal irreducible automorphism of $F_n$.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Andres Robinson Arrieta

item.title: Abelian quotients and orbit sizes for subgroups of linear groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.34680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Keller and Yang formulated two conjectures relating abelian quotients of subgroups of finite linear groups to largest orbit sizes. After counterexamples were found to the original conjectures, two revised versions were proposed. We prove both revised conjectures for every finite group $G$ satisfying $F(G)=F^*(G)$. We also extend a regular-orbit theorem for nilpotent subgroups to completely reducible modules of mixed characteristic under the same hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Yong Yang

item.title: The_Quadratic_Conjecture_and_p-groups_of_maximal_class
item.description: arXiv:2610.34718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Quadratic Conjecture for finite p-groups, which is equivalent to the Strong Oliver Conjecture, asserts that if a finite p-group G acts faithfully on an F-module V, then the center Z(G) contains a quadratic element. In this paper, we investigate the structure of maximal class p-groups and establish that they satisfy the Quadratic Conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Jingjing Duan, Lijian An

item.title: Non-discrete complex hyperbolic $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$-triangle groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.35197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study complex hyperbolic triangle groups of type $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$ with $3\le p_1\le p_2\le p_3\le p_4\le \infty$. We show that if the element $R_1R_2R_3$ is elliptic, then the group is either non-discrete or it belongs to a short list of known discrete groups.
item.dc:creator: Wei Liao, John R Parker

item.title: Modular representations of metabelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.35603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring with unity $R$, and let $\phi:M \to R$ be an $R$-linear map. Then the product $mn = m + (1+\phi(m))n$ defines a monoid $Mon(\phi)$ on $M$. We show that if $G$ is a group, then $G$ arises as the group of invertible elements of some such monoid $Mon(\phi)$ if and only if $G$ is metabelian.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Traldi

item.title: Finite groups with exactly 2p + 1 subgroups of order p
item.description: arXiv:2610.35643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let m_p(G) be the number of elements of order p in a finite group G, p prime. We prove that there is no finite simple group G with m_p(G) = 2p^2-p-1, and that a finite group with this property exists if and only if 2p+1 is prime or 3^f with f an odd prime. This concerns an open problem and extends the classification of finite groups with few elements of prime order.
item.dc:creator: Ihechukwu Chinyere, Bernard O. Bainson

item.title: Infranormal Kazhdan subgroups and instability in finite actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the group $G=\mathbb{Z}[1/2]^3\rtimes(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely presented and residually finite, but is not stable in finite actions, answering a question of Gohla and Thom. The proof uses the infranormal Kazhdan subgroup $H=\mathbb{Z}^3\rtimes\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ and its normal closure $N$ in $G$. A Kazhdan projection estimate shows that, in any $G$-action weakly contained in finite actions, every $H$-invariant measurable subset is also $N$-invariant. We construct an explicit sofic approximation of $G$ whose limit action contains a measurable subset that is $H$-invariant but not $N$-invariant.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Pinke

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi i (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay

item.title: The Symmetry of Differential Neural Tangent Kernel under the Orthogonal Group
item.description: arXiv:2610.34023v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The differential neural tangent kernel (DNTK) is a tool for analyzing the training dynamics of overparameterized physics informed neural networks. In this work, we investigate the symmetry of the infinite DNTK under an orthogonal group, for two layer and deep neural networks separately, based on the explicit expression of the DNTK and recursive formula, respectively. The results are for all activations with or without a bias term, and shed insight into the structure of the infinite width DNTK. Then we prove that the integral operators over the unit sphere induced by operators from the same group orbit share the spectrum, and their reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces differ only by an orthogonal transformation, and that the operator fixed DNTK exhibits zonal symmetry on the unit sphere for symmetric operators. Thus the eigenvalue decay rate of the associated integral operator can be derived for shallow networks with RePU activation and zero bias initialization.
item.dc:creator: Bangti Jin, Longjun Wu

item.title: Local Reflexivity and Exactness for Reduced $C^*$-Algebras of Wreath Products
item.description: arXiv:2610.34695v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every countable non-exact discrete group $H$ and every nontrivial countable discrete group $K$, the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is not locally reflexive. These provide the first known examples of non-locally reflexive reduced group $C^*$-algebras, settling a longstanding existence question. Moreover, for every nontrivial countable exact discrete group $K$, we establish that local reflexivity of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is equivalent to exactness of $H$, and hence to exactness of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$. This gives a partial affirmative answer to Kirchberg's question of whether local reflexivity implies exactness for $C^*$-algebras. As applications, we construct finitely generated groups with the Haagerup property, as well as finitely generated residually finite groups, whose reduced group $C^*$-algebras are not locally reflexive. In particular, neither the Haagerup property nor coarse embeddability into Hilbert space guarantees local reflexivity of the associated reduced group $C^*$-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Pingchuan Dong, Zhe Dong

item.title: Cross work induced by transformations on the symmetric group and related transformation semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.34902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a new permutation statistic, called the \emph{cross work}, on four important subsemigroups of the partial transformation semigroup $\mathcal{PT}_n$: the symmetric group $\mathcal{S}_n$, the semigroup of singular transformations $\mathrm{Sing}_n$, the symmetric inverse semigroup $\mathcal{I}_n$, and the semigroup $\mathcal{POI}_n$ of partial order-preserving injective transformations. The cross work is defined via local distance interactions between adjacent positions and their images. Fundamental invariance properties are established, including inversion invariance under a natural symmetry condition and a characterization of conjugations preserving the statistic. Using elementary combinatorial methods, we derive closed formulas for the total and average cross work on $\mathcal{S}_n$. We also determine the exact minimum and maximum values of the cross work, showing that the maximal value grows quadratically with $n$.
item.dc:creator: Nsibiet E. Udo, Victor A. Owai, Moses O. Francis

item.title: The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings
item.description: arXiv:2610.35222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Capovilla, Alberto Casali, Marco Moraschini

item.title: On Cayley Graphs of Skew Braces and Their Distances
item.description: arXiv:2610.35388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the left and right Cayley graphs of a finite skew brace $(A,\cdot, \circ)$ with a connection set $T\subset A$, as a directed multigraph with additive and multiplicative edges, depicting the operations $\cdot$ and $\circ$ respectively. We compute the distance from $a$ to $a\circ b$ in these Cayley graphs in terms of factorization lengths over $T$. As an application, we provide a characterization of the ideals of a skew brace in terms of their corresponding Cayley graphs.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Syarif Ahdal, Ryan Aziz, Denny Riama Silaban

item.title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.35537v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Ram Karan Choudhary, Harish Kishnani, Anupam Singh

item.title: Cutoff for random walks on nilpotent groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.35561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study continuous-time random walks on finite nilpotent groups, allowing non-symmetric and nonuniform increment measures. Under a simple degree condition, sharp up to an absolute constant factor, we prove that total variation cutoff occurs if and only if the relaxation time is of smaller order than the mixing time. We establish a quantitative reduction to the Abelianization that preserves relaxation times and compares mixing profiles. Combining this reduction with a Gaussian approximation and the third-named author's cutoff criterion for diffusions yields the cutoff characterization.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Hermon, Xiangying Huang, Justin Salez

item.title: Generalizing Praeger--Xu graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.35623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We uniformly study directed Praeger--Xu graphs and Praeger's generalized family $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(\Gamma,r,s)$, without requiring that $s\mid r$ and $\Gamma$ is an undirected graph. Assuming that $\Gamma\times\overrightarrow{K}_2$ is connected, we determine the full automorphism group of $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(\Gamma,r,s)$ for every $r$ and $s$, prove connectivity, characterize vertex-transitivity, and give an equivalent criterion for $t$-arc-transitivity. We also study when $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(\Gamma,r,s)$ is a Cayley graph. We also give two applications. First, we give a new family of twin-free connected arc-transitive digraphs of valency $4$ whose vertex stabilizers have exponential growth. We also give a connected regular digraph that is not vertex-transitive but whose direct product with a directed cycle is Cayley.
item.dc:creator: Zhaochen Ding, Ci Xuan Wu

item.title: Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)
item.description: arXiv:2610.35674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Guoliang Yu

item.title: On the number of epi-, mono-, and homomorphisms of groups
item.description: arXiv:2012.03123v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is known that the number of homomorphisms from a group $F$ to a group $G$ is divisible by the greatest common divisor of the order of $G$ and the exponent of $F/[F,F]$. We investigate the number of homomorphisms satisfying some natural conditions such as injectivity or surjectivity. The simplest nontrivial corollary of our results is the following fact: {\it in any finite group, the number of generating pairs $(x,y)$ such that $x^3=1=y^5$, is a multiple of the greatest common divisor of 15 and the order of the group $[G,G]\cdot\{g^{15}\;|\;g\in G\}$.
item.dc:creator: Elena K. Brusyanskaya, Anton A. Klyachko

item.title: Classification of skew left braces with additive group isomorphic to the infinite dihedral group
item.description: arXiv:2606.29641v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify all skew left braces with additive group isomorphic to the infinite dihedral group. There are ten isomorphism classes.
item.dc:creator: Akihide Hanaki, Yuto Sakata, Hiroki Yoshino

item.title: A characterization of the reversibility of linear cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2608.20600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a group, let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field, and let $V$ be a $\mathbb{K}$-vector space. We prove that there exists a bijective linear cellular automaton $V^G\to V^G$ whose inverse is not a cellular automaton if and only if $G$ is not locally finite and $\dim_{\mathbb{K}}V \geq |\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$. In particular, $|\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$ is the exact dimension threshold for non-reversibility. This answers an open problem proposed by T. Ceccherini-Silberstein and M. Coornaert.
item.dc:creator: Alonso Castillo-Ramirez

item.title: Solvability of unimodular equations in groups and Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.28045v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Our results imply, in particular, that a finitely generated solvable group $G$ is nilpotent if and only if it contains a solution to any unimodular equation, i.e., an equation of the form $\prod g_ix^{n_i}=1$, where $g_i\in G$ and $\sum n_i=\pm1$. A similar fact turns out to be true for Lie algebras. We also exhibit an example of a unimodular equation $w(x)=g$ over a finitely generated group $G$, which has a solution (in $G$) for any $g\in G$, but the solution is not unique for some $g\in G$. We show that, for nilpotent groups $G$, the set of unimodular mappings $G^n\to G^n$ (which are defined naturally) forms a group under the composition.
item.dc:creator: Anton A. Klyachko, Mikhail A. Mikheenko, Alexander Yu. Olshanskii

item.title: On the language of palindromic reduced words in a Coxeter group
item.description: arXiv:2609.29022v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the language of palindromic reduced words in a Coxeter system is regular if and only if the Coxeter group is a direct product of a finite Coxeter group with finitely many copies of the infinite dihedral group.
item.dc:creator: Asilata Bapat

item.title: Finite-color reconstruction of groups and coherent configurations
item.description: arXiv:2609.33938v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Every group has a canonical coloring of its unordered pairs by inverse pairs of differences. We prove that this coloring can be coarsened to four colors without changing its color-preserving permutation group, for groups of arbitrary cardinality. Four is the least uniform bound. A related construction applies to finite homogeneous coherent configurations: if every basic relation has valency at most $d$, where $d\geq 2$, a coarsening with at most $2d+1$ off-diagonal colors in the symmetric case, or $2d+3$ off-diagonal arc colors in general, has the original configuration as its coherent closure. Two-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman refinement recovers that partition within $2\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ rounds on $n$ points, with the specified atomic initialization. Affine-plane schemes show that linear dependence on valency is necessary. We apply the group realization to classify groups admitting naturalizing invariant metrics and show that, for a suitable such metric, naming the identity determines the compatible multiplication uniquely. Finally, using additional Cayley-realization and finite-classification inputs and explicit certificates, we determine the least number of metric values for every group. The direct universal construction and the finite coherent-reconstruction theorem do not depend on those computations.
item.dc:creator: Alex J. Sutherland

item.title: Spectral gap, internality of relative commutants, and non-hyperlinear groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.37761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the relative commutant of a finite unitary tuple in a tracial matrix ultraproduct is internal whenever its conjugation operator has a spectral gap off the commutant. This implies the existence of a non-hyperlinear group.
item.dc:creator: Vadim Alekseev, Jihao Liu, Andreas Thom

item.title: Common non-zero graphs of groups with few edges
item.description: arXiv:2609.39290v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \( G \) be a finite group, and consider its common non-zero graph, which we denote by \( \Gamma_{nv}(G) \). In this graph, the vertices represent the non-linear irreducible characters of \( G \). There is an edge connecting two distinct vertices \( \chi_1 \) and \( \chi_2 \) if there is a vanishing element \( g \in G \) such that \( \chi_1(g) \chi_2(g) \neq 0 \). A finite group \( G \) is described as a strongly \( \mathcal{H}_1' \)-group if the set of vanishing elements of each of its non-linear irreducible character is equal to the set of vanishing elements of \( G \). In this paper, we prove Conjecture 1 from \cite{ourself}, which states that if \( \Gamma_{nv}(G) \) is null (has no edge), then \( G \) must either be a strongly \( \mathcal{H}_1' \)-group or a Frobenius group, whose Frobenius complement is isomorphic to \( Q_8 \). Additionally, we show that if there are no triangles in \( \Gamma_{nv}(G) \), this implies that the group is solvable. We also look at the situation where the common non-zero graph of a finite group \( G \) contains only one edge. This leads us to conclude that \( G \) is either isomorphic to \( S_4 \); or that the single edge in \( \Gamma_{nv}(G) \) is of the form \( \{\theta, \zeta\theta\} \) for some \( \zeta \in \Irr(G/G') \) and \( \theta \in \Irr(G|G') \), $G$ is a $p$-nilpotent group for some prime $p$ and for all characters \( \chi \in \Irr(G|G') - \{\theta, \zeta\theta\} \), we find \( \Van(\chi) = \Van(G) \). Lastly, our study also explores groups whose common non-zero graph forms a star shape, concluding that such configurations can only occur if \( G \) has exactly one non-linear irreducible character.
item.dc:creator: Zeinab Akhlaghi, Sesuai Yash Madanha

item.title: Chord theorems on graphs (revised and extended)
item.description: arXiv:math/0702805v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Horizontal Chord Theorem states that if a continuous curve connects points $A$ and $B$ in the plane, then for every positive integer $k$ there are points $C$ and $D$ on the curve with $\overrightarrow{AB}=k\,\overrightarrow{CD}$. We reformulate the one-dimensional chord problem on finite metric graphs: the \emph{chord set} $\cH(G)$ consists of those $r$ such that every function of mean zero on $G$ integrates to zero over some closed connected subset of $G$ of measure $r$. We prove that the space of connected subsets of fixed measure is compact and path-connected, that $\cH(G)$ always contains the closure of a combinatorially defined \emph{partition set} $\cP(G)$, and that the two sets agree at every rational number; as a consequence, membership of a rational number in $\cH(G)$ is decided by a finite linear program, and the conjecture $\cH(G)=\overline{\cP(G)}$ reduces to a statement about irrational points. We give a covering lemma that yields $\cH(G)=[0,|E|]$ for Eulerian graphs, $[0,1]\subseteq\cH(G)$ when $G$ has no vertex of degree one, and $[0,g(G)]\subseteq\cH(G)$ when $G$ is bridgeless with girth $g(G)$. Conversely, a bridge forces a gap in $\cH(G)$ below $|E|$. Computations on small graphs support the conjecture that $\cH(G)=[0,|E|]$ exactly when $G$ is bridgeless.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Chord theorems on graphs, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 137 (2009), 553--562
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Group-Frames for Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2305.01499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the literature, frames generated by unitary representations of groups (known as group-frames) have been studied only for Hilbert spaces. We conduct the first study of frames for Banach spaces generated by isometrically invertible representations of discrete groups on Banach spaces. These frames are characterized using left-regular and right-regular representations, Gram matrices, and group matrices on classical sequence spaces. A sufficiently large collection of functional-vector pairs using the double commutant of the representation is identified to generate group-frames for Banach spaces. Subsequently, we study Schauder frames generated by time-frequency shift operators on finite-dimensional Banach spaces. We derive the Moyal formula, the fundamental identity of Gabor analysis, the Wexler-Raz criterion, and the Ron-Shen duality in functional form.
item.dc:creator: K. Mahesh Krishna

item.title: Radical subgroups of finite reductive groups
item.description: arXiv:2401.00156v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Radical subgroups play an important role in both finite group theory and representation theory. This is the first of a series of papers of ours in classifying radical $p$-subgroups of finite reductive groups and in verifying the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for them, contributing to the program of proving the Alperin weight conjecture by verifying its inductive condition for finite simple groups. In this paper we present a uniform method for classifying radical subgroups of finite reductive groups. As applications, we investigate the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for classical groups, as well as groups of type $F_4$.
item.dc:creator: Zhicheng Feng, Jun Yu, Jiping Zhang

item.title: Making Space for Time: The Special Galilean Group and Its Application to Some Robotics Problems
item.description: arXiv:2409.14276v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The special Galilean group, usually denoted SGal(3), is a 10-dimensional Lie group whose important subgroups include the special orthogonal group, the special Euclidean group, and the group of extended poses. We briefly describe SGal(3) and its Lie algebra and show how the group structure supports a unified representation of uncertainty in space and time. Our aim is to highlight the potential usefulness of this group for several robotics problems.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Kelly

item.title: Generating pairs in $\mathfrak g_2$ related by an involution
item.description: arXiv:2609.15497v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb O$ be the real octonion division algebra, let $\mathfrak g_2=\operatorname{Der}(\mathbb O)$, and fix a quaternionic subalgebra $H\subset\mathbb O$. We ask when an element $Z$ preserving $H$ and its conjugate $TZT^{-1}$ generate $\mathfrak g_2$, where $T$ is a prescribed involutive octonion automorphism. We prove that such a $Z$ exists if and only if $T(H)\ne H$. Moreover, a fixed set of six derivations preserving $H$ contains a generating choice for every such $T$. For an arbitrary $Z\in\mathfrak g_2$, we construct a polynomial criterion with two factors: one detects reducibility on the imaginary octonions, and the other detects generated algebras of dimension at most three. An irreducible proper generated algebra must be a principal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. We characterize the elements admitting this case by their rotation frequencies and parametrize all corresponding involutions. For one specified involution and quaternionic subalgebra $H$, we describe the nongenerating set by four geometric families and six irredundant systems of scalar equations, and prove that it has real dimension four.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Pineda Montoya, Johan H. R\'ua Mu\~noz, Borut Jur\v{c}i\v{c} Zlobec

item.title: $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless inclusions for the infinite braid group
item.description: arXiv:2609.38596v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $B_\infty$ be the braid group on infinitely many strands and $P_\infty$ its pure braid group. We show that $C^*_r(P_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ and all its intermediate inclusions are $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and completely selfless. This gives natural examples of simple nonnuclear $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $C^*$-algebras. Further examples come from $\mathrm{SL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$. We also show that $C^*_r(\mathbb{F}_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ is completely selfless for the free group $\mathbb{F}_\infty$ of braids in which only the first strand moves. All results hold for twisted group $C^*$-algebras. In contrast, $\mathcal{Z}$-stability fails for $B_n$ with $n$ finite and for groups that are not inner amenable.
item.dc:creator: Tron Omland

item.title: Arbitrary Stage Spectra for Raikov Remainders Along Quotient Towers
item.description: arXiv:2610.02212v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\theta$ be an ordinal and let $(N_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ be a continuous increasing tower of closed normal subgroups of a Hausdorff topological group $G$, with $N_0=\{e\}$. Write $\rho G$ for the Raikov completion of $G$, and put $K_\alpha=\overline{N_\alpha}^{\rho G}$ and $H_\alpha=GK_\alpha$. The successive and limit differences of the groups $H_\alpha$ mark the first stages at which points of $\rho G$ become old quotient points. For every nonzero ordinal $\theta$ and every set $S\subseteq(0,\theta]$, there is a Hausdorff pseudocompact Boolean group with a continuous tower of closed normal subgroups such that every member of the tower is pseudocompact and the nonempty strata occur exactly at the stages in $S$. The terminal quotient can simultaneously be chosen isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, and for every $\delta<\theta$ the successive factor $N_{\delta+1}/N_\delta$ is compact exactly when $\delta+1\notin S$. Thus a tower may have a single nonempty stratum at a limit stage even when every successive factor is compact. For a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, let $\widehat q:\rho G\to\rho(G/N)$ extend the quotient homomorphism and put $K=\overline N^{\rho G}$. Over $gN\in G/N$, the fiber in $\rho G\setminus G$ is $g(K\setminus N)$, homeomorphic to $\rho N\setminus N$, while for $y\in\widehat q(\rho G)\setminus(G/N)$ the entire $\widehat q$-fiber lies in $\rho G\setminus G$ and is homeomorphic to $\rho N$. For precompact kernels this gives a canonical decomposition, and nested quotients give the two-stage identity underlying the transfinite filtration. Further results concern pseudocompact Raikov remainders and include countable Abelian examples.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21940v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $\Gamma$ satisfies $\exp(\Gamma) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.
item.dc:creator: Kengo Enami, Takahiro Matsushita
